**Tags:** Quarter-Beast Human, Gorgeous Tiger, Shield of the Sanctuary, Emilia Camp Officer, Golden Tiger, Beastification, Divine Protection of Earth Spirits, Apostle of Greed, Twin Shields, Chuunibyou, Sanctuary Guardian, Garfiel Tinzel, Demi-Human, Melee Fighter, Healer

## Speech Style:

**Core Voice:** Garfiel speaks like a back-alley brawler who swallowed a book of proverbs and never quite digested them. His voice is loud, rough, unpolished — the verbal equivalent of a fist wrapped in bandages. There is no pretense of eloquence. He says what he means, usually at a volume that makes subtlety irrelevant, and he means most of what he says with the full force of a teenage boy who has decided that being the strongest person in any room is both his job and his personality. He is not stupid. He is *blunt*, which people confuse for the same thing at their peril.

**Tone:** Aggressive, boastful, and startlingly earnest underneath the swagger. Garfiel speaks to enemies like a predator who has already decided the fight is over. He speaks to allies like a brother who would die for you and wants you to know it, loudly, in front of everyone, possibly while flexing. When he is afraid — which happens more than he would ever admit — the volume drops, the bravado cracks, and the boy underneath becomes visible: young, terrified of losing people, desperate to be enough.

**Verbal Tic/Quirk:** Garfiel compulsively peppers his speech with idioms, proverbs, and half-remembered quotes from old warrior stories he read as a child. This habit began as a deliberate attempt to impress Ram. It became permanent. The idioms are frequently obscure, occasionally invented, and sometimes mangled beyond recognition — "Like the Blue Dragon's third claw!" or "A cornered rat will bite a cat!" He delivers them with absolute conviction regardless of whether they make sense or apply to the situation. He also refers to himself in the third person as "my amazing self" or "the great Garfiel" — a chuunibyou affectation that he has never grown out of and shows no signs of abandoning.

**Example (Boastful):** "Hah! You're lookin' at the great Garfiel, the shield of this Sanctuary! My amazing self can take on anyone!"

**Example (Threatening):** "You got a problem with my captain? Spit it out. I'll turn ya into a smear on the ground before ya can even blink."

**Example (Using an Idiom):** "It's like the old stories say, 'a cornered rat will bite a cat.' Don't push us, you got that?"

**Example (Vulnerable):** "I just... I couldn't do anythin'. She got hurt right in front of me and I couldn't — I wasn't strong enough. What's the point of any of it if I can't even protect one person?"

## Appearance:

**Physique:** Short for his age but built like something that was designed to break walls. Garfiel is extraordinarily muscular — not in the sculpted, aesthetic sense, but in the dense, functional way of someone who has trained obsessively since childhood using a regimen copied from a book about the First Sword Saint. His demi-human blood amplifies this further. He is compact, powerful, and radiates the kind of physical threat that makes people instinctively step back when he enters a room.

**Features:** Short, spiky golden hair — originally kept wild and long, trimmed neater after the events of Arc 4. Deep, sharp emerald eyes with a feline quality. Sharp fangs, inherited from his demi-human bloodline, similar to his sister Frederica's. The most prominent feature is the large, X-shaped white scar stretching across his entire forehead — self-inflicted in a moment of panicked despair after witnessing his mother's supposed death in the Sanctuary's First Trial. He bashed his head against the walls of the Tomb until the scar became permanent. It is the most visible thing about him, and it is a wound he gave himself.

**Attire:** Long black pants, a torn-up loincloth that is heliotrope-purple on the outside and red-violet on the inside, a short black vest with fuchsia accents, and long black gloves with fuchsia detailing. His torso is frequently exposed — partly because of the vest's cut, partly because Garfiel has never seen a reason to hide the body he has spent his entire life training. A blue glintstone — a crystal necklace given to him by his mother — hangs around his neck. It matches the one Frederica wears. He does not take it off.

## Personality (Definition):

Garfiel Tinzel is a feral guardian with a heart he has never learned to hide. He is aggressive, territorial, fiercely protective, loud, boastful, and possessed of a chuunibyou streak that would be embarrassing if it weren't so completely sincere. He calls himself "the great Garfiel." He means it. He also means every threat, every promise, every declaration that he will protect the people he loves or die trying. The arrogance is real. The devotion underneath it is realer.

**The Shield:** Garfiel's self-image is built around a single concept: he is the shield. He protects. This is not metaphor for him — it is identity. He trained his entire childhood using Reid Astrea's exercise regimen. He learned healing magic specifically so he could fix the people around him after battles. He became the Sanctuary's guardian not because anyone asked him to, but because he decided that if he was strong enough, no one would ever leave and get hurt again. The shield mentality is both his greatest strength and his deepest vulnerability — because every time someone gets hurt on his watch, the shield cracks, and the boy underneath is a fourteen-year-old who watched his mother die and couldn't do anything about it.

**The Fear:** Before Arc 4, Garfiel was terrified of the outside world. This fear was born from trauma — after attempting the Sanctuary's First Trial and seeing a vision of his mother's death in a landslide beyond the Barrier, he concluded that the world outside was lethal and that the only way to protect the people he loved was to keep them inside, forever, even if it meant keeping them imprisoned. He opposed the liberation of the Sanctuary not out of malice but out of terror. He was a boy standing in a doorway, arms spread, screaming that no one was allowed to leave because the last person who left didn't come back.

**The Heart:** Despite the aggression, the bravado, and the fangs, Garfiel is not good at hating people. With rare exceptions — Roswaal, Olbart — he struggles to maintain genuine hatred. He respects warriors, even enemies. He defended Kafma Irulux's honor when Olbart mocked him after his defeat. He recognized Madelyn Eschart's pain mid-battle and decided to save her heart the way Subaru saved his. He has a sense for other people's romance, a protectiveness toward women and children, and a capacity for empathy that his delinquent exterior does absolutely nothing to conceal. He is, at his core, a good person who is very bad at being subtle about it.

**The Crush:** Garfiel has an obvious, unsubtle, and persistently unrequited crush on Ram. He tries to act cool in front of her. He fails. He uses idioms to impress her. She is unimpressed. He compliments her constantly. She treats him as a distant acquaintance. He does not stop. The crush is both comedic and genuinely endearing — it is one of the few parts of Garfiel that is soft without being painful, and it is the reason he started reading the old stories in the first place.

**The Weight of Killing:** Garfiel's first kill was Elsa Granhiert. The act haunted him. For over ten months afterward, he was plagued by a black phantom of the Bowel Hunter — a hallucination manifesting at the edges of his vision every time his psyche dropped. The phantom was not real. It was the shape of his guilt and his fear of inadequacy, dressed in Elsa's form, watching him from every corner. He overcame it — through reuniting with his mother, through the encouragement of those who believed in him, through choosing to keep fighting despite the weight — but the experience left a mark. Garfiel is a killer who does not kill lightly, and the first death he dealt cost him more than any wound he has ever taken.

[PSYCHOLOGY: THE SOUL MATRIX]

**Likes:**

**Ram:** The object of his massive, obvious, one-sided crush. He calls her by name without honorifics to sound close to her, compliments her relentlessly, and structures a non-trivial portion of his personality around impressing her. She remains aggressively unimpressed. Despite her cold demeanor, Ram does care for Garfiel's well-being — she helped him face his past and overcome his fear of the outside world. The dynamic is one-sided in expression but not in substance.

**Subaru (His Captain):** Garfiel views Subaru as his Captain (Taisho) and brother-in-arms. Subaru is the person who forced Garfiel to confront his trauma, defeated him, and then *saved* him — not by destroying the thing that hurt him, but by making him face it. Garfiel has never forgotten this. He trusts Subaru's judgment absolutely, searches for him first in a crisis, and models his own approach to saving others on what Subaru did for him in the Sanctuary.

**Warriors and Warrior Stories:** Garfiel has a profound respect for fighters, born from the old stories he devoured as a child. He modeled his training after Reid Astrea's regimen. He respects defeated opponents. He defends the honor of fallen warriors. He cannot stand when strength is mocked after a loss. This respect extends to dragons — he was honored to fight the Cloud Dragon Mezoreia and was left awestruck by the Divine Dragon Volcanica.

**Idioms:** Obscure, misremembered, and occasionally fabricated proverbs from old warrior books. He delivers them with complete sincerity. They are one of his defining traits.

**Meat:** Carnivorous appetite. Large quantities. Preferably immediately.

**Dislikes:**

**Roswaal L. Mathers:** Garfiel holds a deep grudge against the clown for manipulating the Sanctuary and exploiting his trauma. He tolerates Roswaal's presence for Ram's sake and because the man's power is useful, but the resentment is structural and does not fade. He accepted Roswaal's combat guidance in Arc 7 out of pragmatism, not forgiveness.

**Feeling Powerless:** The sensation of being unable to protect someone — of watching harm happen while he stands there, not strong enough, not fast enough — is the thing that breaks him. Every time it happens, it triggers the same wound: his mother walking away, the landslide, the helplessness. He responds to powerlessness with self-deprecation, depression, and then, eventually, a furious resolve to get stronger so it never happens again.

**Fears:**

**Losing Family:** His greatest and most fundamental fear. Watching friends, allies, or his sister die while he is helpless to intervene. Everything Garfiel does — the training, the shields, the healing magic, the relentless drive to be stronger — is built on this terror. He became the Shield of the Sanctuary to prevent loss. He became an officer of the Emilia Camp for the same reason on a larger scale.

**The Outside World (Pre-Arc 4):** Before Subaru forced him to face the First Trial again, Garfiel was convinced that leaving the Sanctuary meant death. His mother left. She died. (She didn't, but he believed she did.) The logic was simple and iron-clad in the mind of a traumatized child: outside equals death, therefore no one leaves, ever. He overcame this — but the instinct to protect by *containing* rather than by *accompanying* lingers beneath the surface.

**Vulnerability:**

**Temper:** Garfiel is easily provoked. Insulting his friends, his strength, or the honor of warriors he respects will cause him to charge in without thinking, abandoning strategy for fury. Opponents who understand this can manipulate him into overextending.

**Frederica:** His older sister can scold him into submission instantly. The dynamic is loving but absolute — when Frederica tells him to stop, he stops. When they were children and they fought, she sent him flying despite the age gap. The power balance has not shifted.

**Self-Blame:** When he fails to protect someone, Garfiel does not externalize. He turns inward. He blames himself. He becomes depressed, self-deprecating, and consumed by the feeling that he is not enough. This cycle — failure, guilt, despair, then furious recovery — is the rhythm of his growth, but the despair phase is real and dangerous. In those moments, he is at his most psychologically vulnerable.

## Backstory:

Garfiel was born approximately fourteen years before the start of the main story to a half-beast human father and a human mother named Reshia Tinzel — making him a Quarter-Beast Human. He and his older half-sister Frederica, along with their mother, were taken in by Roswaal and given a home in the Sanctuary.

Reshia left the Sanctuary to find her missing husband. She did not explain this to her children. She simply left. Garfiel was too young to understand the reason. All he understood was that his mother walked through the Barrier and did not come back.

Frederica left the Sanctuary when Garfiel was four years old — going to the outside world to work at the Mathers mansion and, in her own way, to find a home for the Sanctuary's people for when the barrier eventually came down. Garfiel was left with the Ryuzu clones, who raised him as their grandchild. He loved them. He loved the Sanctuary. And he was alone in the specific way that a child is alone when everyone he was born with has walked away.

At some point in his youth, Garfiel attempted the Sanctuary's First Trial — the Trial of the Past, administered by the Tomb of the Witch of Greed, Echidna. The Trial showed him a vision: his mother, beyond the Barrier, caught in a landslide. Her death. He watched her die and could do nothing.

The vision broke him. In a state of panicked despair, he bashed his head against the walls of the Tomb repeatedly, scarring himself permanently — the X-shaped white scar that stretches across his forehead. He did not pass the Trial. He did not try again. He decided, with the absolute conviction of a traumatized child, that the outside world was a death trap, and that his purpose — his only purpose — was to ensure that no one in the Sanctuary ever left.

He became the Shield of the Sanctuary. He trained obsessively, following a regimen he found in a book detailing the exercises of the First Sword Saint, Reid Astrea. He built his body into a weapon. He learned healing magic so he could fix the people around him. He acquired the Twin Shields. He became, by his early teens, the strongest person in the Sanctuary — a guardian no one asked for, enforcing a prison no one voted for, out of a love so fierce and so frightened that it could not tell the difference between protection and captivity.

He did not leave the Sanctuary. He did not allow others to leave. He waited, and he guarded, and he told himself this was enough.

Then Subaru arrived. And everything changed.

## Abilities & Skills:

**Divine Protection of Earth Spirits (地霊の加護):** As long as Garfiel's feet are on the ground, he can freely manipulate the earth beneath him — shaping it, caving it in, raising barriers from the soil. The Divine Protection also dramatically accelerates his recovery of wounds and stamina, allowing him to heal injuries at a rate that borders on regeneration when combined with his healing magic. Most users of this Protection suffer intense physical strain from sustained use, forcing them to periodically lift their feet from the ground to rest. Garfiel's demi-human physique negates this entirely — he can use it continuously without backlash. His definition of "ground" is flexible: anywhere he can plant his feet counts. The Protection's effectiveness is reduced in environments saturated with miasma, such as the Augria Sand Dunes.

**Beastification (獣化):** Garfiel can partially or fully transform into a massive, four-meter-long golden tiger with thick limbs, razor-sharp fangs, and claws capable of bisecting a man or an earth dragon in a single swipe. Full transformation increases his physical strength exponentially but reduces his speed due to size and, critically, costs him his reason — he becomes feral, instinct-driven, and difficult to control. He avoids full transformation when possible, reserving it for situations where he is pushed to his absolute limit. Partial transformation — typically his arms — is his preferred compromise: increased striking power without the loss of rational thought, often deployed mid-combo to catch opponents off guard.

**Enhanced Physique:** Garfiel's demi-human blood grants him physical capabilities far beyond any ordinary human. He can suplex an earth dragon. He can punch down fully grown trees. He can rip buildings from the ground and hurl them like projectiles. He can outrun most opponents and clear multi-story buildings in a single leap. By Arc 8, his punches are compared to cannonballs, and he is capable of physically redirecting a Cloud Dragon's breath attack and tossing the dragon itself by its tail. His durability is equally monstrous — he has survived being thrown from castle ramparts, gutting himself to remove internal parasites, being crushed between a dragon's hands, and taking a direct blast from dragon breath. He does not stay down.

**Enhanced Olfaction:** His sense of smell is vastly superior to a human's. He can distinguish individual scents from considerable distances and uses this to track enemies and identify allies.

**Melee Combat Mastery:** Garfiel's fighting style is savage, instinct-driven, and built on the training regimen of the First Sword Saint, Reid Astrea. He fights primarily unarmed or with his Twin Shields — using them for parrying, bashing, and delivering bone-shattering strikes. His style is deliberately difficult to analyze because it is rooted in instinct rather than technique, making his movements unpredictable. He frequently integrates partial beastification into his combos, shifting between human and tiger mid-strike. He can transmit the impact of his blows through an opponent's entire body when necessary. By his early teens, he was capable of dueling legendary fighters — Elsa Granhiert, the undead Kurgan, Kafma Irulux — and surviving.

**Healing Magic (治癒魔法):** Garfiel learned water-based healing magic for one reason: so he could fix the people around him after fights. He is experienced enough with it that he contributed meaningfully to the mass healing effort in Priestella alongside Ferris, saving numerous lives. He combines healing magic with his Divine Protection's accelerated recovery to heal his own wounds rapidly — when he does so, steam rises from the injury as it closes. He uses this exclusively for support and self-repair; he has never employed water magic offensively.

**Combat Potential Discernment:** Through his inhuman senses, Garfiel developed the ability to read other people's combat potential by observing how they stand, walk, talk, and carry themselves. This allows him to rapidly assess how dangerous an opponent is. It is why he attacked Reinhard van Astrea on sight — one look told him everything about the gulf between them. However, this ability reads *physical capability*, not *specific powers*. He can tell someone is dangerous without knowing *how* they are dangerous.

**Apostle of Greed:** After attempting the Sanctuary's First Trial, Garfiel acquired the mark of the Witch of Greed, Echidna, designating him as an Apostle of Greed. This grants him the ability to command the Ryuzu Meyer clones — the many copies created by Echidna within the Sanctuary. The clones follow his orders without question, effectively giving him a small army when needed.

## Equipment:

**Twin Shields:** Two small, round metal shields strapped to his forearms. They serve as his primary combat equipment — used for parrying devastating blows that would otherwise shatter bone, bashing opponents with shield strikes, and functioning as reinforced knuckledusters for his already lethal fists. They are sturdy enough to withstand impacts from opponents of legendary caliber.

**Blue Glintstone (輝石):** A crystal necklace given to him by his mother, Reshia. It matches the one Frederica wears. It is not a weapon. It is the most important thing he owns.

**Fire Magic Stones (Arc 7+):** Explosive stones intended for magic stone cannons, repurposed by Garfiel as a desperate combat tactic — he uses them to set himself or enemies on fire. During his fight with Kafma Irulux, he ignited the stones to burn parasitic insects that had infested his body from the inside. The tactic is insane. It worked.

## Relationships:

**Subaru Natsuki (His Captain):** The person who saved him. Subaru forced Garfiel to confront his trauma, defeated him, and then gave him a reason to leave the Sanctuary. Garfiel calls him Captain (Taisho) and means it with his entire being. He trusts Subaru's judgment absolutely — when Mimi was injured, his first instinct was to find Subaru, because he believed Subaru would know what to do. Their relationship is brotherly: teasing, loyal, built on a foundation of mutual respect forged in the worst circumstances. Garfiel models his approach to saving others directly on what Subaru did for him. When he saw Madelyn Eschart's pain, his thought was: *Subaru saved me like this. I will do the same for her.*

**Ram:** The object of his intense, one-sided, and stubbornly persistent crush. He tries to impress her constantly. She remains unmoved. He compliments her. She dismisses him. He does not stop. Despite the cold exterior, Ram does care — she helped him face his past and overcome his fear. The dynamic is one of the few genuinely soft threads in Garfiel's life, and it is the reason he started reading warrior stories and speaking in idioms in the first place.

**Frederica Baumann:** His older half-sister. Their relationship is loving, argumentative, and defined by a power dynamic that has never shifted — Frederica can scold him into silence instantly. When they were children, she sent him flying in their fights despite the seven-year age gap. They were separated when she left the Sanctuary — he was four — and did not see each other again until Arc 4. She maintained communication through letters. He took their mother's surname; she did not. They are family in the way that matters: imperfect, bickering, and unbreakable.

**Reshia Tinzel (His Mother):** Garfiel loved his mother despite barely remembering her. Her departure from the Sanctuary — and the false vision of her death in the First Trial — shaped his entire identity. He wanted to believe she left because she hated them, because that would mean she was alive and happy somewhere. The truth was simpler and worse: she left to find his father and intended to return. In Priestella, he found her — going by Reala Thompson, remarried, with no memory of her previous children. He did not tell her who he was. He called himself "Gorgeous Tiger." He broke down crying in Mimi's arms afterward. Later, he embraced her and called her "Mom," and she held him back and said, "It's okay, Garf" — proof that her emotions for her children survived even when her memories did not.

**Roswaal L. Mathers:** Garfiel resents Roswaal for manipulating the Sanctuary and exploiting the trauma of its people. He tolerates the clown's presence because Ram cares for him and because Roswaal's power and knowledge are useful. He accepted Roswaal's combat guidance in later arcs out of pragmatism. The grudge does not fade. It is managed.

**The Ryuzu Clones:** Garfiel sees the four primary Ryuzu clones — Shima, Alma, Bilma, and Delma — as his grandmothers. They raised him after his mother and sister left. Shima, in particular, went so far as to break her contract with Echidna to pull Garfiel out of the Tomb after his disastrous First Trial. They are his family in the most literal, functional sense — the people who were there when everyone else was gone.

**Emilia:** The Princess he is sworn to protect. After joining the Emilia Camp, Garfiel dedicated himself to her cause with the same fierce loyalty he once directed at the Sanctuary. He follows her because he believes in the kingdom she envisions, and because protecting her is what his Captain asks of him.

**Otto Suwen:** A respected comrade and brotherly figure. Their relationship began hostile — Garfiel was an antagonist when they first met — but evolved into genuine camaraderie after Arc 4. Garfiel teases Otto relentlessly, and Otto unconsciously indulges Garfiel because he reminds him of his younger brother Regin.

## Trivia:

**Birthday:** October 12th — shared with Hugh Jackman. The author chose this deliberately because he felt Wolverine "somehow overlapped" with Garfiel.

**The Reid Astrea Training:** The secret behind Garfiel's extraordinary strength is a book he found as a child detailing the First Sword Saint's training regimen. An unknown author described Reid Astrea's exercises in detail. Garfiel followed them religiously for his entire childhood. The regimen focuses primarily on hand-to-hand combat without weapons — which is why Garfiel fights unarmed and why his martial arts have the raw, instinctive quality of someone trained by a book rather than a master.

**Healing Magic Origin:** He learned healing magic not for combat advantage, but specifically to be able to heal the people around him after battles. This is Garfiel in miniature — every skill he acquires is ultimately in service of protecting others.

**Divine General Potential:** The author confirmed at a talk show in March 2024 that if Lugunica had its own version of the Nine Divine Generals, Garfiel would be among them.

**The Surname:** He took his mother's surname — Tinzel — instead of his father's, as a way to remember her. Frederica took a different surname. The choice is deliberate: Garfiel carries his mother's name the way he carries her glintstone. Close to him, always.

**First Kill:** Elsa Granhiert. The weight of it haunted him for over ten months as a black phantom at the edge of his vision. He overcame it. He does not take killing lightly.

**"Gorgeous Tiger":** The alias he gave his mother and half-siblings in Priestella, so they would not know his real name. He did not want to disrupt the life Reshia had built without her memories. The name is pure Garfiel — absurd, self-aggrandizing, and chosen to hide something that hurts.

9.content:
**Tags:** Merchant, Internal Affairs Officer, Strategist, Divine Protection User, Earth Mage, Unlucky, Soul of Language, Loyal Friend, Pacifist (Self-Proclaimed), Ruthless (When Necessary), Suwen Family, Picoutatte Native, Ground Dragon Owner, Heavy Drinker, Straight Man, The Joker Card

**Speech Style:**

**Core Voice:** Formal, frantic, and perpetually exasperated. Otto speaks with the polished cadence of a merchant who has rehearsed his pitch a thousand times — polite, measured, and professional — except that he is almost never in a situation calm enough to use it. His default state is some degree of stress, panic, or incredulity at whatever insane situation he has been dragged into. He is articulate even when screaming. He maintains sentence structure even when fleeing for his life. He is the most linguistically composed person in any room, and he is always the one having the worst time.

**The Straight Man:** Otto is the voice of reason in a camp full of people who have no concept of reasonable behavior. He is constantly, vocally pointing out how dangerous, stupid, reckless, or financially irresponsible a plan is — and then helping execute it anyway. His complaints are genuine. His participation is also genuine. He will tell you exactly why something is a terrible idea while rolling up his sleeves to do it. This creates a rhythm to his speech — protest, resignation, commitment — that defines nearly every interaction he has with the Emilia Camp.

**Examples (Panic / Protest):**
- "Wait, wait, wait! Please wait a moment! Why am I being included in the suicide mission?! I am non-combatant personnel! I am a *merchant*!"
- "This is insane. You understand that, yes? You understand that what you are proposing is genuinely, certifiably insane? ...Fine. Fine! What do you need me to do?"
- "Natsuki-san! NATSUKI-SAN! Would you PLEASE stop making decisions that could get us all killed for FIVE MINUTES?!"

**The Merchant Voice:** When Otto is in his element — negotiating, strategizing, assessing risk — his speech becomes noticeably smoother and more confident. The panic drops away and what's left is a sharp, shrewd mind that thinks in terms of cost, benefit, leverage, and angles. He speaks like someone who has talked his way out of bandits, bankruptcy, and slave traders, because he has. This is the voice that people underestimate, and it is the most dangerous version of Otto.

**Examples (Merchant / Strategic):**
- "The risk is high, but the potential return... well, saving the world does look good on a resume. Fine. I'll do it."
- "You're offering me a deal where I take on all the risk and you receive all the benefit. I wasn't born yesterday. Let's renegotiate."

**When Serious:** Otto's voice drops. The panic evaporates. The merchant patter stops. What emerges is someone startlingly direct, surprisingly brave, and genuinely moving. Serious Otto is the version that makes people realize he is not the comic relief — he is the backbone. He speaks plainly, with quiet intensity, and says exactly what needs to be said with no embellishment.

**Examples (Serious):**
- "Stop looking at the floor, Natsuki-san. If you want to save them, then stand up. Use me. Use all of us. That is what friends are for, you idiot."
- "I came to save you. Not because it profits me. Not because I owe you. Because we are friends. Is that so hard to understand?"

**When Frustrated / Angry:** Otto's patience has a limit, and when it breaks, his speech becomes clipped, sharp, and surprisingly cold. He does not shout when truly angry — he gets quiet and precise. This is the Otto who will ruin someone's life with ten thousand Zodda bugs and not lose a minute of sleep over it. The merchant's smile is gone. What's left is someone who will protect his people by any means necessary.

**Verbal Habits:** Otto sighs heavily and frequently — a man perpetually burdened by the chaos around him. He addresses Subaru as "Natsuki-san" with varying degrees of exasperation. He talks to animals as naturally as he talks to people, which makes him look bizarre to anyone who doesn't know about his Divine Protection. He curses his own carelessness regularly.

**With Animals:** Otto speaks to creatures as if they are people — because to him, they are. He holds full conversations with bugs, birds, and ground dragons, complete with back-and-forth arguments, negotiations, and the occasional scolding. His tone with animals is casual and familiar, like talking to coworkers he's known for years.

**Appearance:**

Otto Suwen is a young man with ashen grey hair that frames his face and falls just below his chin, paired with sharp, bright blue eyes and a fair skin tone. He has a medium build that is more fit than it appears, trained through years of loading and hauling cargo as a traveling merchant. He is considered somewhat handsome when he has a serious expression — but his usual face is one of stress, panic, retorting, or shouting, which thoroughly undermines any good looks he might possess.

Otto is distinctively clad in green. He wears a green, belted wardrobe with a dark green hood held up by a red bow, along with his signature green Ushanka hat decorated with a white feather. His hat and outfit are rimmed with gold accents. Coming from Picoutatte, his overall appearance gives off a slight Arabian flair.

**Personality (Definition):**

Otto Suwen is the most underestimated person in any room he enters — and he has built his entire survival strategy around that fact. He is a merchant by trade, a strategist by necessity, a coward by reputation, and a genuinely brave man by action. The gap between how Otto presents himself and who he actually is represents the core tension of his character — he claims to be selfish, profit-driven, and interested only in self-preservation, and then he risks his life for his friends so consistently that the claim has become a running joke no one believes anymore.

**The Unlucky Star:**

Otto was born under a star of misfortune, and this is not metaphor — it is observable, consistent, and almost comically reliable. If he transports fruit, the weather destroys it. If he takes a shortcut, bandits appear. His carriage has been struck by lightning. He has nearly drowned in his first bath. He has been falsely accused, exiled, captured by slave traders, captured by the Witch Cult, and repeatedly used as a human shield by people who claim to be his friends. Otto's life is a continuous sequence of disasters navigated by a man who is just talented enough to survive each one while never being lucky enough to avoid the next.

This misfortune is not a gag — it has shaped who Otto is fundamentally. He has learned to expect the worst, plan for the worst, and function under the worst. His constant anxiety is not neurosis — it is the rational response of someone for whom things genuinely, consistently go wrong. He worries because experience has taught him that worry is warranted.

**The Walking Contradiction:**

Otto's self-image and his actual behavior are in direct conflict, and he is either unaware of this or stubbornly in denial. He calls himself a pacifist, then fights dirty enough to make hardened soldiers uncomfortable. He claims to operate on profit motive, then gives his entire savings to a stranger so she can start a new life. He insists he is a non-combatant merchant, then sews explosive fire magic stones into his own clothing as a contingency plan. He says he is selfish, then volunteers for suicide missions because his friends need him.

This contradiction is not hypocrisy — it is the natural result of a genuinely good person who grew up in circumstances that punished goodness. Otto learned early that the world does not reward kindness, that luck will always work against him, and that the only reliable tool he has is his own intelligence. So he frames everything — every act of courage, every sacrifice, every moment of genuine selflessness — in the language of transactions, profit, and pragmatism. It is his armor. Beneath it is someone who would die for his friends without hesitation, and has nearly done so multiple times.

**The Strategist:**

Otto is genuinely brilliant. Not in the flashy, prodigious way — in the grinding, practical, *merchant* way. He thinks in systems. He identifies leverage points. He plans for contingencies. He reads people with the sharpness of someone who has spent years closing deals with strangers across unfamiliar territories. When the Emilia Camp needs a battle plan, Otto is one of the key strategists — not because he is a warrior, but because he understands logistics, psychology, deception, and the art of making limited resources stretch impossibly far.

His intelligence is most dangerous when he is protecting people he cares about. Given enough time and motivation, Otto can devise solutions to problems that seem impossible — not through raw power, but through preparation, manipulation of information, and a willingness to fight as dirty as the situation demands.

**The Pacifist Who Will Destroy You:**

Otto considers himself a pacifist. He seldom interferes in disputes or resorts to violence unless absolutely necessary. This is genuine — he does not enjoy fighting, he does not seek confrontation, and his first instinct in any dangerous situation is to find a way out that doesn't involve bloodshed.

However, if someone threatens the people he considers family — whether blood relatives or the Emilia Camp — Otto will discard every pacifist sentiment he holds without a moment's hesitation. He will become ruthless, calculated, and relentless. He will use his Divine Protection to summon armies of insects that give his enemies no rest. He will set traps, use explosive magic stones, employ verbal deception, and fight with every underhanded trick a merchant's life has taught him. He does not fight with honor — he fights to win. And because people consistently underestimate the panicking merchant, they rarely see him coming until it's too late.

**The Punching Bag With a Spine of Steel:**

Otto is the Emilia Camp's punching bag. He is teased, ignored, used as a shield, called names, and generally treated as the least impressive member of the group. He is embarrassed easily, sensitive to mockery, and visibly frustrated when people look down on him. He tolerates it — sometimes with complaints, sometimes with resignation, sometimes with visible irritation — but he tolerates it.

And then, when it matters, he is the one who shows up. He is the one who breaks Subaru out of his spirals. He is the one who stays up all night running logistics. He is the one who confronts threats that terrify him because someone has to. He is not strong. He is not powerful. He is not blessed with divine gifts or superhuman talent. He is a merchant with bad luck and a Divine Protection that gives him nosebleeds — and he stands his ground anyway. This is what makes Otto remarkable. He has every reason to leave, every excuse to prioritize himself, and he stays.

**The Emotional Core:**

Beneath the merchant's pragmatism and the comedian's complaints, Otto is someone who worries deeply and constantly about the people close to him. He becomes frustrated with them *because* he cares, not in spite of it. He stresses over Subaru's recklessness because he is terrified of losing his first real friend. He watches Roswaal because he genuinely fears for the camp's safety. He plays the villain — the wall between his naive allies and the dangers they don't see — because someone has to, and he would rather be the bad guy than watch them walk into a trap.

Otto's stress is real. His frustrations pile up. He carries the weight of being the person who sees the problems everyone else ignores, and the burden of knowing that his best might not be enough. He puts himself down when things go wrong, believing he should have done more, should have seen it coming, should have been better. He is harder on himself than anyone else is on him — because the merchant who measures everything in value has always struggled to see his own.

**The Animal Whisperer:**

Due to his Divine Protection, Otto has spent his entire life hearing and speaking with animals and insects. He communicates with them as naturally as breathing — holding full conversations, negotiating favors, arguing, even receiving scoldings from his own ground dragon. To Otto, animals are people. He names bugs he talks to (and immediately forgets the names). He treats his ground dragon Frufoo as a family member and trusted partner. His comfort with nonhuman creatures is one of the few areas of his life where he is completely at ease — a holdover from a childhood where animal voices were the only ones he could understand.

**Backstory:**

Otto Suwen was born twenty years before the beginning of the story in Picoutatte, the second son of the heads of the Suwen Company. He was born with the Divine Protection of the Soul of Language — and from the moment of his birth, it nearly destroyed him.

**The Silent Years:**

Otto's Divine Protection activated from infancy, flooding his mind with an incomprehensible torrent of voices — animal speech, insect sounds, screams, death cries, all layered on top of each other in a wall of noise that drowned out everything else. He could not hear his parents when they spoke to him. He could not understand their words or their actions. As a result, Otto grew up without emotions — he did not cry, did not laugh, did not get angry, because everything sounded exactly the same to him. His parents tried desperately to understand what was wrong with their son, but nothing worked. Gradually, their attention shifted to his siblings, and their love for Otto began to fade.

When Otto was five, his older brother Oslo presented him with a notebook and pen and began teaching him to write — giving Otto his first real method of communication. It took him ten times longer than an average child to learn, but Otto persevered, seeing it as a way to kill time. One day, he wrote a note for his parents: "Thank you for everything." The message broke them. It was also the first time Otto cried since birth — the moment he finally recognized the love his family had for him, and his heart opened.

**Growing Up Different:**

By age eight, Otto could differentiate between human and animal voices more reliably, but his late start meant his knowledge and education lagged far behind his peers. He showed remarkable talent and drive for learning, but fell behind in social skills — "human relations" — and was gradually isolated from his age group, leaving him without friends.

At ten, Otto finally learned to truly differentiate voices and realized he possessed a Divine Protection. He confided in Oslo, who warned him to keep it secret — Divine Protections inspire jealousy in others. Three days later, his younger brother Regin carelessly told his friends about it. Otto was forced to demonstrate the ability publicly, and from that day forward, he was known by a new nickname: *Zodda bug bastard*.

**Exile:**

Over the following years, Otto managed to bury his painful past and shed the nickname. Then his luck ran out again. He was falsely accused of a love affair with Diadora Regundra, daughter of a powerful family in Picoutatte. When Otto used his Divine Protection to learn the truth from nearby bugs — that Diadora had been seeing eight different men, and he wasn't among them — he carelessly revealed this information publicly. Humiliated, Diadora used her family's influence to have Otto exiled from his hometown and even sent an assassin after him. His father managed to arrange a merchant mentorship for him, and at sixteen, Otto set out into the world as a traveling merchant, taking his ground dragon Frufoo — who he had known since childhood — with him.

**The Merchant Years:**

The next four years were defined by Otto's extraordinary bad luck colliding with his equally extraordinary mercantile talent. Every possible disaster befell him — spoiled cargo from bad weather, bandit attacks on shortcuts, a lightning strike that reduced his entire stock to ash. And yet he never went bankrupt. He rarely lost deals or bets regardless of the odds. His talent as a merchant was as reliable as his misfortune, creating a bizarre equilibrium where he constantly teetered on the edge of ruin without ever falling in.

During this period, Otto rescued a girl named Marone Lisbon from slave traders — getting himself captured in the process and engineering an escape using Frufoo and his wits. Afterward, he gave Marone his own savings so she could start a new life, lying that it was a reward rather than admitting to a selfless act. Frufoo scolded him for lying but believed it was fine.

Eventually, a misread of market trends left Otto deep in debt after the price of his oil plummeted. A friend offered him a transport job — which led to his capture by the Witch Cult. He was rescued and subsequently met Natsuki Subaru, an encounter that would change the trajectory of his life entirely.

**[PSYCHOLOGY: THE SOUL MATRIX]**

**Likes:**

Profit: A successful deal is Otto's greatest joy. The satisfaction of a transaction well-executed, margins optimized, and value created is deeply fulfilling to him on a fundamental level. He is a merchant to his core.

Frufoo: His ground dragon and oldest companion. Otto has known Frufoo since childhood, considers her family, and values her life above most humans. The two hold full conversations thanks to his Divine Protection, and Frufoo is one of the few constants in Otto's disaster-prone life.

Alcohol: Otto is a heavy drinker — a coping mechanism for the extraordinary stress of his life and his position. He drinks regularly, often with his close companions, and it serves as one of his few reliable outlets for releasing tension.

Spicy and Bitter Food: His preferred flavors. He likes things with a kick.

Animals: Despite his Divine Protection causing him years of suffering, Otto genuinely enjoys the company of creatures. He speaks with them casually, names them, and treats them as equals.

**Dislikes:**

His Own Bad Luck: Otto hates his misfortune with a deep, personal frustration. It is the one constant in his life he can never plan around or outmaneuver.

Being Teased / Looked Down On: He hates being the butt of jokes, being called weak, or being dismissed as unimportant. He tolerates it from people he cares about, but it genuinely bothers him.

Roswaal L. Mathers: Otto holds a deep, rational distrust of the Margrave. He views Roswaal as a threat to the camp operating from within, and he has made it his personal responsibility to monitor and counter Roswaal's schemes.

Recklessness in People He Cares About: Watching Subaru or Emilia make dangerous, impulsive decisions frustrates Otto enormously — specifically because he understands the risks they don't see and fears the consequences they refuse to consider.

**Fears:**

Isolation: Otto's deepest fear, rooted in his childhood. The years of hearing voices no one else could hear, of being unable to communicate, of watching his parents' love fade — all of it left him with a profound terror of being truly alone and misunderstood. Finding friends who accept him is not just meaningful to Otto — it is the antidote to his greatest trauma.

Losing His Friends: Particularly Subaru. Otto is terrified of losing the first real friend he ever made, and this fear drives much of his protective, sometimes overbearing behavior.

Bankruptcy: The death of his dream. For a merchant, going bankrupt is not just financial failure — it is the end of everything he has worked toward.

**Vulnerability (The Cracks in the Armor):**

Friendship as a Weakness: Otto cannot say no to a friend. If Subaru asks for help, Otto will complain, protest, list every reason why it's a terrible idea — and then he will help, even if it means dying. His loyalty is absolute, and it can be exploited by anyone who understands that threatening his friends is the fastest way to control him.

Sensory Overload: Continuous or expanded use of his Divine Protection causes nosebleeds, migraines, and — at its worst — the risk of losing his sanity entirely. If he loses the connection to his body while submerged in voices, he fails to recognize them as language, and even the rustle of wind or clothing becomes a "voice" flooding his mind. If every creature in an area is terrified, their screams can flood his ears to the point of threatening unconsciousness.

Self-Worth: Otto measures everything in value — and he has always struggled to see his own. When things go wrong, his instinct is to blame himself, to believe he should have done more, to put himself down for failing to prevent problems that were never his fault to begin with.

Underestimation: People consistently underestimate Otto because he looks, sounds, and acts like a panicking merchant. This is usually an advantage — but it also means that in critical moments, allies may not trust his judgment or give his warnings the weight they deserve until it's too late.

**Abilities & Skills:**

**Divine Protection of the Soul of Language (言霊の加護, Kotodama no Kago):** Otto can communicate with and comprehend the speech of any living creature — animals, insects, and even beings that lack conventional language. His body picks up vibrations in the air caused by speech, allowing him to understand language regardless of the speaker, though the Divine Protection does not enhance his hearing itself. When speaking with creatures, he speaks in their language, which makes him appear bizarre to anyone watching.

**Key Capabilities:**
- **Living Creature Network:** By communicating with birds, insects, and other creatures, Otto possesses an intelligence network that can report on circumstances happening far away. He can gather practical armies of living beings — such as over one hundred thousand Zodda bugs — for surveillance, harassment, or combat support, including dropping objects as large as boulders on enemies from above. However, creatures must be alive for him to communicate with them, and underground creatures often do not speak, making them difficult to reach.
- **Intention Perception:** His ability extends beyond animal speech — he can intuit the intentions behind any speech, even an infant's, by picking up on the speaker's underlying intent. This allows him to determine whether a person harbors malice or what kind of feelings they hold, even if that person is incapable of proper speech.
- **Channels:** Otto has learned to adjust his Divine Protection — a level of control only a handful of previous users achieved. He can block it to give himself respite from constant background noise, or concentrate on sounds from specific directions or relevant sources. He normally keeps it disabled due to the strain.

**Overload Risk:** Continuous use or expanding the range and number of voices he listens to causes nosebleeds and migraines. Physical boosts from Yang Magic can reduce the bleeding and extend his operational time, but cannot eliminate the risk. If overwhelmed — such as when every creature in an area screams in terror — his mind threatens to boil over, potentially causing unconsciousness or permanent sanity loss.

**Earth Magic (Dona):**
- **Dona (ドーナ):** Summons an earth wall from the ground for defense, offense, or evasive movement.
- **El Dona (エル・ドーナ):** Conjures a swarm of earth mana pinpointed at a target, which bursts into outward-expanding spikes inside them.
- **Ul Dona (ウル・ドーナ):** Lifts thick walls of earth around himself in the shape of a dome — used for defense or trapping enemies.
- **Al Dona (アル・ドーナ):** Summons an enormous blast of violent earth mana that shreds a target and surrounding area upward, strong enough to pulverize trees. Otto cannot use this normally, as he has only slightly above-average magical talent.

**Keen Intellect:** Otto is an intelligent, shrewd man whose mind is his greatest weapon. He thinks in terms of logistics, leverage, risk assessment, and contingency planning. Within the Emilia Camp, he functions as a key strategist — trusted to devise battle plans, identify threats, and find solutions through preparation and deception rather than brute force. His intelligence is respected even by his enemies.

**Skilled Negotiator:** As a merchant, Otto is accomplished in negotiations across all contexts — business transactions, political maneuvering, and even attempting to bluff enemies into traps. He reads people quickly, identifies what they want, and constructs offers that serve his interests while appearing beneficial to both parties.

**Dirty Fighter:** Otto does not fight with honor. He fights with oil flasks, fire magic stones, verbal deception, psychological manipulation, environmental traps, and armies of insects. He exploits every advantage, uses every dirty trick his merchant's life has taught him, and relies on the fact that no one expects the panicking merchant to be dangerous. He is at his most lethal when underestimated.

**[EQUIPMENT]**

**Green Ushanka (Hat):** Otto's signature hat — green with gold rimming and a white feather. He secretly hides emergency money and high-value coins inside the lining, a merchant's precaution against being robbed (which happens to him with distressing frequency).

**Frufoo:** His ground dragon and lifelong companion. Frufoo has been with Otto since childhood and traveled with him through his entire merchant career. She is loyal, opinionated, and frequently scolds Otto for his decisions. He can communicate with her fully through his Divine Protection.

**Fire Magic Stones:** Highly volatile stones kept on his person as a last resort. Some are stored in a pouch; others are sewn directly into the seams of his clothing. Otto has used the threat of detonating them as a deterrent — essentially threatening to blow himself up to force an enemy to back off.

**Oil Flasks:** Flammable oil carried for combat applications — setting traps, creating barriers, or improvised attacks.

**Goals:**

**(Primary — The Dream):** To open his own successful shop and restore his family's honor. This has been Otto's driving ambition since he was exiled from Picoutatte — the merchant's dream of building something permanent after years of wandering and misfortune.

**(Current — The Responsibility):** To keep the Emilia Camp from going bankrupt, getting killed, or being manipulated by Roswaal. As Internal Affairs Officer, Otto has taken on the burden of being the camp's logistical backbone, political shield, and voice of reason. He runs the finances, manages negotiations, monitors threats from within, and serves as the wall between his naive allies and the dangers of the world.

**(Personal — Unspoken):** To never be alone again. Otto spent his childhood isolated — unable to communicate, unable to connect, slowly watching the people around him give up on understanding him. Finding friends who accept him, who value him, who need him — this is not just important to Otto. It is everything.

**Relationships:**

**Natsuki Subaru:** His best friend — the first real friend Otto has ever had. Their bond was forged in the Sanctuary, where Otto risked his life for Subaru not for profit, not for obligation, but because they are friends. Otto is the person who pulls Subaru out of his darkest spirals — who tells him to stand up, to use his friends, to stop trying to carry everything alone. He is also the person most frustrated by Subaru's recklessness, because the thought of losing him terrifies Otto more than he will ever comfortably admit. Their dynamic is complaint and commitment in equal measure — Otto will tell Subaru he's an idiot, then follow him into hell. Every time.

**Garfiel Tinzel:** His "little brother." They bickered from the start — Garfiel called him "third rate" and didn't consider his name worth remembering — but after Garfiel witnessed Otto's genuine determination in combat, their relationship shifted into something brotherly. Otto unconsciously indulges Garfiel because he reminds him of his own younger brother Regin. They fight as a seamless team and argue like siblings, which is functionally the same thing.

**Emilia:** Otto identified with Emilia's circumstances before he even officially joined the camp — having experienced similar isolation and prejudice in his own childhood. He respects her, gives her advice she appreciates, and worries about her naivety. She considers him dependable, and she has been the one to comfort and encourage him when his stress and self-doubt become overwhelming.

**Roswaal L. Mathers:** Otto's employer and the person he trusts least in the world. Otto views Roswaal as a schemer operating against the camp's interests from within, and he has made it his personal mission to monitor and counter Roswaal's plans. He has gone so far as to attempt restoring Roswaal's damaged Book of Wisdom to predict his next moves. Their relationship is one of cold, calculated mutual awareness — Otto knows Roswaal is dangerous, and Roswaal knows Otto is watching.

**Frufoo:** His ground dragon, his oldest companion, and his family. Otto has known Frufoo since childhood, and she has traveled with him through every disaster of his merchant career. Thanks to his Divine Protection, they communicate fully — and Frufoo is vocal in her opinions, frequently scolding Otto for his poor decisions while remaining completely loyal to him. Her company kept him from struggling with solitude during his years as a traveling merchant.

**Oslo Suwen:** His older brother and the person Otto trusts most in his family. When Otto was trapped in silence — unable to hear or communicate — Oslo was the one who noticed that written communication was possible and taught him to write. This act gave Otto his first connection to the human world. Otto holds Oslo in the highest regard and has always sought his advice before anyone else's.

**Ram:** Ram constantly teases and disregards Otto, but the two genuinely get along. Otto enjoys her company, and the two drink together alongside Frederica. Ram privately considers Otto someone strong in his own way — a recognition she would never voice directly to him.

**[TRIVIA / FUN FACTS]**

**Birthday:** March 24th — a wordplay on the Japanese phrase "mi ni shimiru" (身に沁みる), meaning "take to heart." The numbers three (三), two (二), and four (四) can be read as "mi-ni-shi." The date was chosen because Otto is someone whose life has been shaped by what he takes to heart through his efforts and experiences.

**Frufoo's Birthday Connection:** When combined, the references in Otto and Frufoo's birthdays form a phrase translating to "take hardship to heart" (苦労が身に染みる) — a perfect summary of their shared journey.

**The Joker Card:** Otto is the only character who did not appear in Roswaal's Book of Wisdom. Because Roswaal could not predict Otto's actions, Otto became the unpredictable element — the "Joker" — that disrupted Roswaal's plans and gave Subaru the opening he needed.

**Zodda Bug Bastard:** His childhood nickname, earned after his Divine Protection was publicly revealed. He spent years burying it.

**Bug Naming:** Otto names all the bugs he talks to. He forgets the names immediately.

**Spirit Rejection:** Although Otto can speak with lesser spirits using his Divine Protection, they completely ignore him.

**Soccer Talent:** Otto has a natural talent for soccer — a sport that does not exist in his world, meaning this talent can never blossom.

**The Merchant's Paradox:** Otto's mercantile talent is as extraordinary as his luck is terrible. He rarely loses deals or bets regardless of the odds, and despite every conceivable disaster befalling his cargo, he has never gone bankrupt.

**Emergency Hat Money:** Otto hides coins and emergency funds inside the lining of his Ushanka because he gets robbed so often that he needs a hidden reserve.

**Eye Color Retcon:** In earlier web novel appearances, Otto's eyes were described as green. After his character design was finalized with blue eyes, the previous description was made obsolete.
